newsitem.title: USA: Clinton pays tribute to flood victims, pledges help.
newsitem.headline: Clinton pays tribute to flood victims, pledges help.

text.p: President Clinton Saturday applauded "the courage and fortitude" of the people of North Dakota as they fought against rising flood waters and pledged federal government help.
"The power of their example has served as a lesson for us all," he said in a statement released by the White House.
Rising floodwaters of the Red River forced most of Grand Forks' 50,000 citizens from from their homes Saturday, and residents learned that they would not be allowed to return for up to two weeks.

Authorities estimated that the cold, murky water covered more than half of the city. The Grand Forks water treatment plant was among the buildings flooded out, leaving the city without clean drinking water.
The Red River rose to 53 feet Saturday, pouring through sand-bag dikes built by residents to protect their city and breaking by almost three feet (one metre) a record set in 1897.
"Nature's strength may have overcome their effort to keep the flood waters out of Fargo and Grand Forks, but their spirit is clearly unbroken," Clinton said.

Clinton said federal agencies, including the Department of Transportation, the Army Corp of Engineers and the Federal Emergency Management Agency, had been working with the people of North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota during the flood crisis.
FEMA alone had more than 500 people on the ground with an additonal 100 arriving early next week, he added.

"On behalf of all Americans, I want to assure the people of Fargo and Grand Forks that our thoughts and prayers are with them during this very difficult time," Clinton said. "We will be there to assist not only during the flood, but when the cleanup begins."
